newsitem.title: USA: CFTC reform seen as top issue for US Senate panel.
newsitem.headline: CFTC reform seen as top issue for US Senate panel.

text.p: The top priority for the Senate Agriculture Committee this year will be passage of revisions to the basic U.S. law governing commodity traders, committee chairman Richard Lugar said Wednesday.

Lugar told reporters he hoped to include changes to the so-called Treasury amendment. It was created in 1974 to exempt interbank foreign-exchange trading from jurisdiction by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
There have been complaints that unscrupulous traders have abused the exemption. The CFTC, Treasury Department and others have wrangled for weeks over fashioning a narrower exemption.
"We'll have to do that ourselves in the event the agencies cannot work it out," the Indiana Republican senator said. "I would like to settle the Treasury amendment dispute," he added.
No date has been set for filing the bill, but Lugar said a version would be introduced in time for hearings scheduled for February 11 and 13.
An aide to Lugar said there were signs of progress on compromise language on the Treasury amendment.
The bill sought by Lugar would speed up approval of new contracts and cut some regulation of U.S. exchanges.
"The purpose of the legislation is to strength American markets," Lugar said.

After the so-called CFTC bill, Lugar said the committee's priorities for the year would be reauthorization of agricultural research programs and tax reform, particularly estate and capital gains taxes.

Iowa Senator Tom Harkin, the Democratic leader on the panel, said he was interested in improving the federal "safety net" for farmers and in nutritional programs. The Clinton administration has said it will try to expand food stamp coverage as part of amending the new welfare law.
